Metadata-driven Data Asset Inventory & D.description_en:
In today's digital workplace, information has become a strategic asset that must be safeguarded and managed properly. This course provides a practical guide to the information management (IM) methods, tools and activities that support an effective departmental IM program. Participants will learn how to use a function-based classification structure, establish retention specifications and follow the proper process for disposing of information resources.

Topics include:

• applying function-based methodologies 

• documenting practices and procedures 

• developing retention specifications to facilitate the disposition process

Prerequisites:

Information Management: Supporting Programs and Services (I230) is a prerequisite for this course.

Notes:

This course is divided into three 3 hour sessions scheduled over a one-week period.
Metadata-driven Data Asset Inventory & D.title_fr: Méthodes et outils de gestion de l'information (COR509)
Metadata-driven Data Asset Inventory & D.description_fr:
Dans l'environnement de travail numérique d'aujourd'hui, l'information est devenue une ressource stratégique qui doit être protégée et gérée adéquatement. Ce cours présente de façon concrète les méthodes, les outils et les activités de gestion de l'information (GI) qui favorisent l'efficacité des programmes ministériels de GI. Les participants apprendront à utiliser une structure de classification basée sur les fonctions, à établir des critères de conservation et à suivre les démarches appropriées pour éliminer des ressources documentaires.

Sujets traités :

• appliquer des méthodes axées sur les fonctions; 

• consigner les pratiques et les procédures; 

• établir des critères de conservation afin de simplifier le processus de disposition.

Préalables :

Le cours La gestion de l'information à l'appui des programmes et des services (I230) est un préalable à ce cours.

Remarques :

Ce cours est divisé en trois séances de 3 heures réparties sur une semaine.

The Agile method for project management works best when a project team is cohesive, productive and engaged, with a clear understanding of project requirements and stakeholder expectations. This online self-paced course offers insights into the characteristics of agile project teams and team leaders, and recommends strategies to help improve team performance and cohesion. Participants will learn about communication tools and developmental mastery models in Agile, as well as the benefits of using facilitation techniques like games to foster collaboration and cooperation.

- identifying strategies for achieving stakeholder commitment
- engaging stakeholders through the five phases of the Agile Project Management model
- reviewing decision-making techniques and tools
- describing the characteristics of a cohesive and effective team

Trade-off and Prioritization Criteria.title_en: CAPM®: Development Approach and Life Cycle Domain (TRN347)
Trade-off and Prioritization Criteria.description_en:
As a project manager, determining the right approach to take is critical to a successful project. This online self-paced course presents the predictive, adaptive and hybrid approaches to project development and their intended outcomes. Participants will review project variables and organizational considerations when selecting a development approach, and their interactions with the life cycle performance domain.

 

Topics include:

- reviewing various project development approaches
- identifying best practices for aligning project cadence, approach, and life cycles
- recognizing the interactions between the development approach and life cycle performance
- acknowledging result-based considerations when determining a project approach

 

Notes:

This course is intended for all public servants, including those with or without project management experience. Materials are aligned with the PMBOK® Guide – Seventh Edition.

Completion of the 26 courses in the CAPM® course series can count towards the eligibility requirements for the Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM®) exam administered for a fee by the Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
The CAPM® exam is not administered by the Canada School of Public Service. Learners wishing to take the exam are responsible for validating their eligibility directly with PMI.

Advanced Data Privacy and Legal Risk Ass.title_en: Project Management and the Senior Leader (TRN415)
Advanced Data Privacy and Legal Risk Ass.description_en:
The complexity of projects within the Government of Canada has increased significantly in recent years, along with the risks and challenges faced by project leaders. This course for senior executives at the EX-04 and EX-05 levels focuses on how to lead, oversee and enable complex projects in the federal ecosystem. Through in-class discussions, case studies and reading assignments, participants will be given opportunities to enhance and improve their knowledge, capacity and networks when leading projects, making decisions and providing project oversight.

Topics include:

· setting a strong foundation: understanding key project management roles and considerations

· disciplined execution: establishing quality relationships with stakeholders and within project teams

· illustration and reflection: reflecting on what makes a project a success or a failure

Notes:

This course requires a commitment of approximately 30 hours, spread out over the week.

This course is intended for senior executives at the EX-04 and EX-05 levels who play a role in project management, including as senior project sponsors, business owners, senior designated officials and central agency officials.

Registration for this course is available by invitation only.

Advanced Data Privacy and Legal Risk Ass.description_fr:
La complexité des projets au sein du gouvernement du Canada a considérablement augmenté ces dernières années, tout comme les risques et les défis auxquels sont confrontés les chefs de projet. Ce cours, destiné aux cadres supérieurs de niveau EX-04 et EX-05, porte sur la façon de diriger, de superviser et d'activer des projets complexes dans l'écosystème fédéral. Au moyen de discussions en classe, d'études de cas et de lectures, les
participants auront l'occasion de renforcer et d'améliorer leurs connaissances,
leurs capacités et leurs réseaux lorsqu'ils dirigent des projets, prennent des décisions et assurent la supervision de projets.

Sujets traités :

· définir des bases solides : comprendre les rôles et les considérations clés de la gestion de projet;

· assurer une exécution rigoureuse : établir de bonnes relations avec les intervenants et au sein de l'équipe de projet;

· recueillir des exemples et faire une réflexion : réfléchir aux éléments qui mènent à la réussite ou à l'échec d'un projet.

Remarques :

Le cours nécessite un engagement d'environ 30 heures, réparties sur la semaine.

Ce cours s'adresse aux cadres supérieurs de niveau EX-04 et EX-05 qui exercent des fonctions liées à la gestion de projet, notamment en tant que promoteurs principaux de projet, responsables de secteur d'activité, hauts fonctionnaires désignés et responsables d'organismes centraux.

L'inscription au cours est sur invitation seulement.
